analysis.title: GS Duttenhoefer - Duttenhoefer's Daily 23.10.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 121bps to 7663 (+12% YTD) in a clear AI risk-off move. Nasdaq fell 2.9%. 65 S&P stocks fell more than 4%, while 337 stocks were higher.
Tech sold off sharply after Meta earnings: Lam -13%, Ciena -11%, Meta -7%. Meta's 5-year CDS is much higher. GS's AI basket (GSTMTAIP) is down 23% since June.
Defensive rotation: Staples +3% and Healthcare +2%. Volumes were strong and VIX rose 14%.
US 10-year yield reached 4.96%, the largest one-day move in 2026. Brent is at $114 on escalation fears, Gold at $4004 and Bitcoin at $81k. Earnings next week include Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet.

The GS US team continues to favor the broadening trade. SPXXAI outperformed the SPX by 6% in October and is closing the gap. The correlation of AI (GSTMTAIP) with SPXXAI is falling. AI is about 50% of the SPX, and 45% of SPX names have negative beta to the index.
SOX has underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over the last 9 sessions, its biggest stretch of underperformance in 20+ years. It is testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025.

AI spending concerns: a WSJ analysis found roughly $3tr of off-balance-sheet AI commitments in August, including $1.2tr in leases. S&P Global warned that interconnected AI financing could leave additional liabilities.

The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell 0.3m barrels to 283m, the lowest since October 1982. Persian Gulf oil exports have reportedly surpassed prewar levels under an improvised, US-protected shipping system.

GS analyst Eric keeps a positive view on Meta and raised the price target to $885 from $860. Family of Apps engagement, user growth and ad revenue remain strong. Muse is emerging as a consumer agentic platform, and shopping with Muse is used by more than 25% of Muse weekly active users, with average purchases above $200. AI compute buildout remains a spending priority.
GSXUBOND Index (48 stocks) is a clean equity expression of a long-duration view.

GS does not expect a 2022-style energy crisis in European gas. Reasons: higher ex-Mideast LNG supply, more LNG import capacity in NW Europe, more nuclear and renewable generation, lower gas demand, and reduced government intervention.

The EU Quality pair (GSPEQUAL, High Quality GSXEHQLT vs Low Quality GSXELQLT) returned +8% over the past month after a long period of underperformance. GS sees substantial room for further outperformance and a catch-up trade.
The top 10 contributors are expected to account for 68% of S&P 500 earnings growth in 3Q26 (vs 48% in 2Q26). Micron and Nvidia together account for 34% of index growth.

As of midday Thursday, GS PB had Fundamental L/S down 1.1%, Systematics down 1.2% and Multi-Strats down 1.4%. It was the first time since Covid that all three fell more than 1% on the same day. 155 S&P names had 2-sigma moves, the most since May 2025.
Unconstrained Momentum (GSPRHIMO) is having its worst drawdown since the GFC, excluding the Covid period.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $885 from $860. Core engagement, user growth and ad revenue remain strong and are increasingly AI-driven. Management said Muse monetization may come earlier than past products.

sector_views.rationale: Heavy underperformance after Meta earnings, with the AI basket down 23% since June and SOX testing its 200-day moving average. GS still favors the broadening trade over AI concentration.
The Quality pair returned +8% in a month. GS sees room for a catch-up trade based on low leverage, high profitability and earnings stability.

Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet report next week, and the market is focused on them after the Meta reaction.
